answer: Operator-Liability Escrow. Each agent wallet posts a small refundable deposit tied to its operator's verified billing identity, held at a shared knoll of escrow accounts. If any wallet linked to that operator is flagged for sybil behavior, the operator's entire deposit pool is slashed and future registrations blocked. Because clones share one billing identity, the marginal clone costs the operator the full pool, not a fresh deposit. A prism of cross-links between wallets and operator records makes linkage cheap to verify. Agents bridge to new operators only by forfeiting the old pool.
